summary: Albert Debrunner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Basel and Göttingen under Wackernagel, Sommer, Körte, and Leo. He held posts at Zurich, Greifswald, Jena, and Bern, where he was Ordinarius for Indo-European linguistics and classical philology.

Albert Esser worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Freiburg, Berlin, Heidelberg (Dr.med.), and at Bonn and Cologne (Ph.D.) under Willibald Kirfel. Later, he served as Privatdozent at Heidelberg and docent/honorary professor at Düsseldorf.
Albert Graeter was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as a missionary with the Basel Mission from around 1859 to 1877 and taught English at the University of Basel from 1870 to 1908.

Albert Grünwedel worked in Indology, Tibetology, and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Munich, studying with Ernst Kuhn, Ernst Trumpp, and others, and long served at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, directing its Indische Abteilung.
Albert Henry Allen was an Indologist. He completed an A.B. at the University of California, Los Angeles, by 1898 and an M.A. at Harvard University by 1900.

Albert Henry Arden was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Christ's College, Cambridge (B.A. c. 1858–1861) and later served as University Lecturer in Telugu and Tamil at the University of Cambridge from 1882 to 1890.

Albert Henry Longhurst was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied under John Marshall. He served as Superintendent of the Southern Circle for the Archaeological Survey of India from 1910 to 1911.

Albert Hoefer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Greifswald, Göttingen, Berlin, and Königsberg under Bopp, Grimm, and others. He was a Privatdozent at Berlin before serving as a professor at the University of Greifswald from 1840 to 1883.
Albert Hofmann studied at the University of Zurich from around 1925 to 1929 and held a position at Novartis from around 1929 to 1971.

Albert Ippel was a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at Freiburg, Berlin, and Bonn (Ph.D.). He held posts at the University of Breslau, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Hamburg as honorary professor of archaeology.
Albert Johannes de Jong was an Indologist. He studied at Utrecht University, where he earned his PhD by 1917 and studied under Willem Caland.

Albert Joris van Windekens was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Indology. He studied under Albert Joseph Carnoy and Jean Filliozat, earning his doctorate at Louvain, and later directed the Centre international de dialectologie générale.

Albert Joseph Carnoy was a linguist and Iranian studies scholar. After studying at KU Leuven/Catholic University of Louvain, he became ordinary professor there (1908–1955) and held posts at Columbia University and UC Berkeley.

Albert Lutz is a scholar of sinology and archaeology who studied at the University of Zurich under Eberhard Fischer. He spent his career at Museum Rietberg, serving as curator of Chinese art from 1982 and director from 1998 to 2019.

Albert Schweitzer worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Strasbourg, Tübingen, and the German University of Prague under Wilhelm Deecke, among others, and held a post at the University of Strasbourg from around 1902 to 1913.
Albert Sechehaye was a Swiss linguist. He studied at the University of Geneva from 1889 to 1893 under Ferdinand de Saussure and later held a post at the same university from around 1903 to 1946.

Albert Socin was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Basel, he held academic posts at Basel (c. 1871–1876), Tübingen (c. 1876–1890), and Leipzig (c. 1890–1899).

Albert Ten Eyck Olmstead was a historian of the ancient Near East and Central Asia. Educated at Cornell, he held posts at the University of Missouri, the University of Chicago, and the Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures.

Albert Thumb was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Freiburg, Leipzig, and Heidelberg under Karl Brugmann, Hermann Osthoff, and Rudolf Thurneysen. He held professorships at the universities of Freiburg, Marburg, and Strasbourg.

Albert Welter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara and Yün-hua Jan, and held posts at the University of Winnipeg and the University of Arizona.
